selection: first 15 distinct blocked_identity tokens encountered in rank order; first refusals only, not all missing reactants
method: Read-only exact-source registry/parser/material/adapter review; no CLI/API execution, builds, alias additions or chemistry implementation
common_requirements: Endpoint/chemistry prerequisite work precedes identity implementation as ordered by the current task.
Preserve original frozen scripts, first refusals and expectations; corrected protocols and source bindings are separate.
Alias admission must preserve exact composition, charge, phase, canonical serialization, registry collision protection, recipe revisions and finite stock accounting.
A successful parser/identity repair does not establish a reaction, product identity, rate, energy, yield or physical validation.
Never silently supply a counterion, solvent, catalyst, pressure, isomer, hydrate or substitute stock.

records.evidence: The registry admits Na+ aqueous ion, NaCl and NaOH, but no elemental Na. Dataset requires neutral solid Na, not a sodium-containing reagent.
next_lane: Admit a sourced Na(0) solid identity, mandatory thermophysical properties and finite water-reaction scope.
Test actual Na/water hydrogen, hydroxide, matter and energy budgets separately from input admission.
paired_acceptance: Na must stay distinct from Na+, NaCl and NaOH; no charge-changing alias.
After species admission, compare matched neutral Na feeds across text/direct/JSON; retain missing reaction limits until validated.

records.evidence: Neither ethanal nor acetaldehyde/CH3CHO is a registered identity. Existing ethanol and propanone differ in structure/composition.
next_lane: Add a structure-bound ethanal identity and sourced properties before proposing acetaldehyde naming aliases.
Prepare Tollens reagent and aldehyde oxidation only after silver-complex/free-ligand ownership and reaction conditions are supported.
paired_acceptance: Ethanal/acetaldehyde may be paired only after their same molecular identity is sourced.
Reject ethanol, ethylene oxide and other C2H4O isomer substitutions; formula equality alone is insufficient.

records.evidence: Br- and HBr exist; neutral molecular Br2 does not. Source phase is solution without a solvent/concentration specification.
next_lane: Add molecular Br2 with sourced phase/properties and a declared finite dissolved-bromine preparation.
Specify solvent, dose and light/radical conditions for a separate ethene bromination replay.
paired_acceptance: Br2 must remain distinct from Br- and HBr.
Paired pure/dissolved feeds require explicit solvent and conservation accounting, not an automatic phase alias.

records.evidence: No tristearin identity exists. Vegetable oil and coconut fat are unresolved material surrogates; fatty_soap is a role-based equivalent, not a molecular triglyceride.
next_lane: Admit the specified C57H110O6 triglyceride with sourced identity, phase and properties.
Extend finite multi-ester hydrolysis and glycerol/stearate product ownership with defined aqueous/base conditions.
paired_acceptance: Do not alias tristearin to vegetable_oil, coconut_fat, triolein or ethyl_acetate.
A named pure triglyceride and a recipe containing it must preserve the same molecular dose; unresolved oil is a separate negative control.

records.evidence: I2 and KI are registered; Lugol solution is an explicit I2/KI/water material recipe. No triiodide ion or iodide/polyiodide speciation identity is admitted.
next_lane: Add charge-correct I3- and its iodide/iodine equilibrium only with sourced constants and analytical ownership.
Define the starch/polyiodide observable separately from finite molecule/charge balances.
paired_acceptance: Do not alias I3- to I2, KI or lugol_solution_1_percent.
Any declared Lugol follow-up must preserve its actual I2/KI/water composition and remain separate from the frozen I3- protocol.

records.evidence: The source specifies no formula, charge, sequence or chain length. Gelatin and albumin are material surrogates with unresolved protein content, not molar peptide species.
next_lane: Choose and source a concrete peptide/sequence or explicitly version a non-stoichiometric teaching material before defining amounts.
Scope copper-peptide complexation and the biuret observable for that declared entity.
paired_acceptance: Do not silently turn 0.001 mol peptide into gelatin/albumin grams or glycine.
Require identity/chain-length-sensitive positives and a declared non-peptide negative control; no generic pseudo-formula.

records.evidence: No glycine identity exists in the registry. Source C2H5NO2 neutral formula alone does not supply amino-acid microstates or dehydration conditions.
next_lane: Add structure-bound glycine with sourced phase/properties and explicit acid/base microstate ownership.
Separate peptide bond formation conditions, product identity and water balance from simple aqueous glycine admission.
paired_acceptance: Do not alias to a glycine cation, an unrelated C2H5NO2 isomer, gelatin or a generic peptide.
After admission compare same-identity glycine spellings; charge-state inputs must remain independently balanced.

records.evidence: Pb metal and Pb+2 exist, but no PbO2 solid identity is admitted. Those existing identities do not represent Pb(IV) oxide.
next_lane: Add phase-specific sourced PbO2 and PbSO4 identities/properties before a lead-acid cell domain.
Define both electrodes, acid/sulfate inventory and finite current/discharge boundary; contact alone is not an electrical protocol.
paired_acceptance: PbO2 must not alias Pb, Pb+2 or an arbitrary lead salt.
Positive/negative electrode controls must conserve Pb/S/O/H/charge and distinguish lead oxidation states.

records.evidence: Existing CuSO4 is solid CuSO4, M=159.609 g/mol, with white-when-dry optical data. Chalcanthite is separately registered CuSO4·5H2O, M=249.684 g/mol.
next_lane: Add only the exact anhydrous naming alias through the shared species identity boundary after endpoint prerequisite acceptance.
Keep hydration/chalcanthite reaction and observable acceptance separate from successful naming.
paired_acceptance: add v1 CuSO4_anhydrous 0.001mol must canonicalize identically to add v1 CuSO4 0.001mol across text/direct/JSON/save-replay.
Negative: chalcanthite must retain distinct hydrate formula, molar mass and blue-crystal identity; no recipe/stock duplication or dry/hydrated collapse.

records.evidence: The registry has CO2(aq) with formula CO2, not H2CO3. PROTONATION_SPLITS maps native MINTEQ H2CO3 onto CO2(aq) with solvent completion; that readback basis conversion is not an input synonym.
next_lane: First declare whether input means molecular H2CO3 or the existing dissolved-neutral-carbon analytical convention.
If an explicit hydrated species is added, preserve its extra H2O stoichiometry and sourced hydration/protonation model.
paired_acceptance: Never directly alias H2CO3 to CO2(aq) or CO2 gas: their formulas/phase and water coordinates differ.
A separately declared analytical mapping must account for one water per hydrated molecule and compare C/H/O/charge; physical molecular fractions remain a separate claim.

records.evidence: The dataset explicitly requires C2H3O2 charge -1. Existing CH3COO- is the aqueous acetate ion with that formula/charge and M=59.045 g/mol.
next_lane: Add an exact acetate -> CH3COO- alias through all shared identity boundaries after endpoint prerequisites.
Keep complete-stock acetate hydrolysis controls separate: bare anion input remains an analytical component with its charge limitation.
paired_acceptance: add v1 acetate 0.001mol must match add v1 CH3COO- 0.001mol in canonical identity, inventory and warnings across text/direct/JSON/save-replay.
Negative: CH3COOH, NaOAc and ethyl_acetate remain distinct; NaOAc supplies an actual sodium counterion and cannot be inferred.

records.evidence: NaHSO4 and SO4-2 are registered, but HSO4- is not. The existing sulfate/proton analytical convention does not admit an explicit bisulfate feed. Vendored wateq4f explicitly defines H+ + SO4-2 = HSO4-; native availability alone does not create a runtime registry identity.
next_lane: Add a source-bound HSO4- aqueous identity and verify adapter master/protonation/readback accounting.
Use native thermodynamic support only after checking explicit H/O/charge and avoiding double-counted proton equivalents.
paired_acceptance: HSO4- must not alias SO4-2, NaHSO4 or H2SO4.
Once admitted, explicit Na+ plus HSO4- should agree with complete NaHSO4 under identical conditions; standalone ion retains incomplete-charge disclosure.

records.evidence: No salicylic_acid identity exists; source specifies ortho-hydroxybenzoic acid, C7H6O3. Acetic anhydride is a further unresolved reactant in the same frozen protocol.
next_lane: Add structure/position-specific salicylic acid with sourced properties; do not infer identity from gross formula.
Prepare acetic anhydride/aspirin identities and a condition-complete acetylation endpoint as separate acceptance.
paired_acceptance: Positive salicylic acid naming pairs need a verified ortho structure.
Reject 3-/4-hydroxybenzoic acid or other C7H6O3 isomers as aliases; acetic acid is not acetic anhydride.

records.evidence: No chloroethane identity exists. Bromoethane is registered C2H5Br, not C2H5Cl; source chloroethane phase is gas.
next_lane: Add structure-bound C2H5Cl with sourced gas/phase properties and finite gas/liquid handling.
Scope hydrolysis conditions and chloride/ethanol products separately; do not infer kinetics from a wait command.
paired_acceptance: Chloroethane/ethyl chloride names may be paired only after source-backed identity admission.
Bromoethane, ethanol and ethene are negative identity controls; gas feeds cannot be silently replaced with liquid moles at an invented density.

records.evidence: No propene identity exists. Existing propane is C3H8; ethene is C2H4; isobutylene is 2-methylpropene C4H8. None is C3H6 propene.
next_lane: Add sourced propene/propylene structure and gas properties first.
Prepare 2-bromopropane and condition-gated ionic HBr addition/regioselectivity, preserving radical-condition limits.
paired_acceptance: Verified propene/propylene naming may later be paired; reject propane, ethene and isobutylene aliases.
Products/conditions must distinguish 2-bromopropane from 1-bromopropane rather than matching a gross formula.
